summary.headline: Dabur's new India CEO Herjit Bhalla rates vision pillars 18 months in, flags M&A as red and plans 150-200 bps extra A&P investment funded by efficiencies.
summary.overview: This was an analyst/investor meet held on November 5, 2026, after the Q2 FY27 results, in which India CEO Herjit Bhalla reviewed the 18-month mark of Dabur's 3-year vision across seven pillars. He reported consolidated revenue growth of 11.6% and India standalone growth of 8.9%, with India FMCG up 10.7% (volume 5.5%, price 5.2%) and the international business growing about 20%. He self-rated the pillars: green for Saksham go-to-market, simplification and operating efficiencies; amber for core brands and health and wellness; red for strategic M&A. Management said it is pulling forward a medium-term plan to 2031, to be presented in 6 to 8 months, and launched an internal "Ignite" programme.

financial_highlights.change: second consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth
fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit PAT growth
inflation largely in HPC, mostly mitigated
described as a strong recovery; non-supplement healthcare in teens
up from 17% over 18 months; growing 4x overall rate
distributor attrition down ~80%, throughput up 2x, ROI up 30%

segments.name: HPC (India)
segments.commentary: Grew at double-digit despite input inflation; management said bulk of inflation was absorbed. Skin (Oxy DeTan, Gulabari), home care (Odonil) and new categories (car and automatic diffusers) cited as growth areas.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 6.9%; health supplements remain challenged, Chyawanprash needs revival, while OTC and digestives (Hajmola, Pudin Hara, Isabgol) grow strongly.

segments.name: Foods and beverages (F&B)
segments.commentary: Foods growing strong double digits; beverages bounced back on a good season, with premium Real Activ and coconut water growing strongly.

segments.name: Alternate channels
segments.commentary: Strong double-digit growth; general trade back to growth for two quarters, with the best GT growth in about 19 quarters this quarter.

segments.name: Badshah (acquired)
segments.commentary: Management said it continues to deliver robust growth; no figure given.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Growing about 20%; runs independently, overseen by Mr Narang.

guidance_outlook: Full-year double-digit growth guidance reiterated; first two quarters delivered slightly ahead of that pace, with momentum to be maintained.
Plan to add 150-200 bps of extra A&P/media investment, targeted at core brands with the highest expected return.
Savings target: 1.5x the INR 115 crore delivered under Project Samriddhi, i.e. INR 170-200 crore (management interpretation).
Premiumization target raised to 23% of portfolio over the next 18 months, possibly sooner.
Sesa to be integrated into Dabur from December 1, with retrospective effect from April 1.
Medium-term strategy with a 2031 plan to be presented in the next 6-8 months; the earlier next vision was due March 2028.
capex_capacity: Ignite programme (launched ~3 months ago) focuses on energising the core, scaling stars, execution excellence, future-ready portfolio and funding these investments.
Retail Next programme across 40,000 stores targets growth 1.5x that of the rest of GT; direct coverage of 100,000+ villages planned, geotagged.
IRIS initiative launched for continuous replenishment and forecasting accuracy.
Dabur Ventures formed October 2025; first investment RAS made earlier in 2026.
Monofloral (lychee) honey launch due later in November; premium honey runs at 2.5x normal honey cost.
Management said India-level capital war chest is almost INR 6,000 crore, available for acquisitions at the right valuation.
demand_pricing: India FMCG volume growth 5.5% and pricing 5.2% in Q2, implying a sharp price-led contribution.
Management described consumption as challenging given the Middle East conflict, crude-driven inflation and elevated inflation, with HPC inflation the main pressure.
Calibrated price increases and mix improvement cited as levers to protect margins.
Chyawanprash had a strong winter loading; new TVC and gummies launched to address relevance with younger consumers.
Beverages: Real Activ 100% juices growing at strong double digits with market share gains; nectars core weaker.
Quick commerce described as complementary to GT for premium and innovation lines.
Dabur Shop and Siens by Dabur (nutraceutical D2C brand) are early-stage D2C efforts.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of moving M&A from red to green in 18 months, given peers' acquisitions and the need for disruptive products and D2C?
qa_highlights.answer: Herjit Bhalla declined to commit to an 18-month timeline, citing high valuations. M&A must be adjacent to existing categories, with no new categories, and must offer synergies and the right valuation. D2C is nascent (Dabur Shop, Siens), and the higher end of Sesa's portfolio may strengthen it.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a new group CEO, and are the earlier consultants continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: No new global CEO; the board sees current structure as adequate. Bhalla joined the board, and the international business runs independently under Mr Narang. McKinsey was part of Vision 7; a decision on continuation will be made within about a month.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the growth capital for investments come from, and will EBITDA flow-through be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ankush Jain said operating efficiencies across mix, production and procurement would fund most needs, with possible gross margin upside next fiscal. The INR ~6,000 crore war chest is available for synergistic acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Does 'sharpening the saw' mean more portfolio streamlining?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. SKUs and brands are being reviewed on size and profitability, either to enhance profitability or exit, as an ongoing exercise. 6 brands and 350 SKUs have already been removed.

qa_highlights.question: Why not target 15-20% growth rather than double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhalla said Dabur is not maintaining the status quo and is advancing its strategic exercise. Some pockets can deliver 20-50% growth, but he gave no company-level target above double digit.

qa_highlights.question: Where should incremental growth come from across healthcare, foods and HPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhalla named health and wellness as the priority, particularly OTC and digestives, with foods and premium beverages and HPC skin and home care as other focus areas. Jain noted non-supplement healthcare grew in the teens.

qa_highlights.question: Is the chemist channel getting focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. A chemist programme is part of Project Saksham, with MSL and digitisation used to get the right portfolio into the right stores, particularly for OTC and digestives.

qa_highlights.question: Can Chyawanprash and nectars be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Chyawanprash revival relies on a new communication, gummies for younger consumers, and distribution; a TVC alone is not the answer. Honey is the template: purity, traceability, occasion-based usage, premium variants and sampling.

risks_watch: M&A pace: self-rated red; any deal must clear strategic fit and valuation discipline, and the timeline was explicitly not committed.
Margin pressure from HPC inflation and crude-linked costs; the 150-200 bps A&P step-up must be funded by efficiencies.
Health supplements remain challenged and Chyawanprash growth has been flat for 3-4 years, per an analyst.
Sustainability of GT momentum after Saksham distributor consolidation.
Sesa integration from December 1, 2026, with retrospective effect from April 1, 2026.
Medium-term 2031 plan due in 6-8 months, and the content of any reset strategy.
summary.management_tone: Candid and self-critical in the scorecard (amber and red ratings), with confidence on execution and Saksham. Evasive on M&A timing and on a specific growth ambition beyond double digit.
key_quotes: We've now delivered two quarters where our growth on GT has been mid-single digit growth.
I will not lock us into an 18-month timeline. I think that would be unfair to the team.
We're going to look to invest 150 to 200 basis points of advertising and promotion extra, or media investments that go further in those areas.

growth.why: Management reiterated double-digit FY27 revenue growth after H1 running slightly ahead, backed mainly by price-led FMCG growth (5.2% price), premiumisation and a 150-200 bps A&P step-up plus INR 170-200 crore savings target; no specific new capacity or orders were quantified, so backing is vague.

mgmt.note: Herjit Bhalla is the new India CEO (joined within roughly the last 18 months) and is pushing a 3-year vision with pillars, Ignite programme and 2031 medium-term plan.
initiatives: Ignite programme for core energising, scaling stars and execution excellence
Retail Next across 40,000 stores and direct coverage of 100,000+ villages
Premiumisation to 23% of portfolio within 18 months
Pulled-forward medium-term plan to 2031 in 6-8 months

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin dilution held to 10 bps in India standalone, and management says efficiencies may give possible gross margin upside next fiscal, but 150-200 bps extra A&P step-up will absorb much of it and HPC inflation persists.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or stores quantified; Retail Next targets 40,000 stores and 100,000+ villages but no capacity addition timing was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India FMCG volume grew 5.5% in Q2 and management says momentum will be maintained after H1 ran slightly ahead of double-digit guidance, though volume is only about half of the 10.7% growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the INR ~6,000 crore war chest is earmarked for acquisitions, not capacity, and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated only double-digit FY27 growth and declined to set a company-level target above double digit, despite H1 running slightly ahead.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumption described as challenging with Middle East conflict, crude-driven inflation and HPC input pressure, and the A&P step-up adds cost risk to the double-digit guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Monofloral lychee honey launch due later in November, plus new Chyawanprash TVC and gummies and new car and automatic diffusers, with premium share targeted at 23% within 18 months.

rows.label: INR 170-200 crore savings target
rows.why: 1.5x the INR 115 crore delivered under Project Samriddhi, funding most of the 150-200 bps extra A&P step-up via mix, production and procurement efficiencies.

rows.label: Sesa integration from December 1, 2026
rows.why: Sesa integrates into Dabur from 1 December 2026 with retrospective effect from 1 April 2026, so it will show up in reported numbers from the next quarter.

rows.label: Medium-term 2031 plan pulled forward
rows.why: Management is presenting a plan to 2031 in 6-8 months, earlier than the March 2028 vision date, with M&A still rated red and no timeline committed.

tone.note: Management was confident on Saksham, the 43% distributor consolidation and the 2x throughput, and on premiumisation (20% share); it was cautious on M&A timing (red rating, no 18-month commitment) and declined a growth target above double digit. Analysts pushed on M&A, Chyawanprash and nectar revival
